previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with lower abdominal pain and found to have peritoneal dialysis-associated peritonitis, supported by elevated peritoneal fluid white blood cell count of 305 with 15% polymorphonuclear cells. She had recently stopped antibiotic prophylaxis due to a suspected allergic reaction. Initial treatment with IV vancomycin and cefepime was transitioned to intraperitoneal vancomycin and ceftazidime after clinical improvement and irrigation of the peritoneal cavity. Cultures and gram stains remained negative, but clinical and laboratory markers improved over the course of admission. She was discharged home to complete a 14-day course of intraperitoneal antibiotics with instructions for dwell technique and follow-up. Chronic conditions including type 1 diabetes, gastroparesis, and end-stage renal disease were managed with home medications throughout.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ is a ___ year old woman with ESRD on PD, T1DM, HTN, 
HLD, recent episode of peritonitis currently on IP 
Vancomycin/ceftazidime, readmitted with worsening abdominal pain 
likely secondary to ongoing peritonitis (improved on IP 
vanc/ceftaz) and worsening gastroparesis in the setting of 
poorly controlled diabetes and constipation.
 
#) PERITONITIS:
Pt with recent PD-associated peritonitis who was readmitted with 
worsening abdominal pain despite one week of IP antibiotics with 
ceftazidime and vancomycin.  Initial peritoneal fluid concerning 
for recurrent peritonitis (WBC 730 with 13% PMNs); however, 
repeat peritoneal fluid reassuring with only 14 WBCs.  Repeat 
peritoneal cultures have shown no growth to date.  Pt was 
started on oral fluconazole given initial concern for fungal 
peritonitis, but this was discontinued after the fungal cultures 
returned negative.  Pt was also continued on IP vancomycin and 
ceftazidime, these were discontinued on ___ per Renal recs.

#) GASTROPARESIS:
Pt developed worsening gastroparesis in the setting of poorly 
controlled diabetes, constipation and peritonitis.  
Gastroparesis was managed through controlling blood sugars (as 
below), and aggressive bowel regimen.  Pt was continued on home 
Domperidone, and restarted on Reglan with close QTc monitoring.  
Pt was also managed symptomatically with Ativan and Zofran.  

# ESRD on PD:  
Pt was seen by renal dialysis consult during admission.  Pt was 
continued on PD during admission.  Started on sevelamer during 
admission.

#) T1DM:

with lantus and Humalog sliding scale.  Pt was seen by ___ 
consult during admission, and regimen was adjusted.

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast

INDICATION:  History: ___ with ESRD on peritoneal dialysis status post recent
diagnosis of peritonitis on IP vanc/ceftaz presenting with LLQ abdominal pain,
nausea, and diarrhea // evaluate for diverticulitis or other intrabdominal
source of infection

TECHNIQUE:  Single phase split bolus contrast: MDCT axial images were acquired
through the abdomen and pelvis following intravenous contrast administration
with split bolus technique.
Oral contrast was not administered.
Coronal and sagittal reformations were performed and reviewed on PACS.

DOSE:  Found no primary dose record and no dose record stored with the sibling
of a split exam.
!If this Fluency report was activated before the completion of the dose
transmission, please reinsert the token called CT DLP Dose to load new data.

COMPARISON:  ___ CT abdomen/pelvis
___ CT abdomen/pelvis

FINDINGS: 

LOWER CHEST: Visualized lung fields are within normal limits. There is no
evidence of pleural or pericardial effusion.

ABDOMEN:

HEPATOBILIARY: There are scattered small locules of pneumoperitoneum, most
prominent over the dome of the liver. The liver demonstrates homogenous
attenuation throughout.  There is no evidence of focal lesions.  There is no
evidence of intrahepatic or extrahepatic biliary dilatation.  The gallbladder
is within normal limits.

PANCREAS: The pancreas has normal attenuation throughout, without evidence of
focal lesions or pancreatic ductal dilatation.  There is no peripancreatic
stranding.

SPLEEN: The spleen shows normal size and attenuation throughout, without
evidence of focal lesions.  There is a 1.6 x 0.9 cm locule of fluid adjacent
to the spleen of without peripheral enhancement.

ADRENALS: The right and left adrenal glands are normal in size and shape.

URINARY: The kidneys are atrophic, but with normal nephrogram.  There is no
evidence of focal renal lesions or hydronephrosis.  There is no perinephric
abnormality.

GASTROINTESTINAL:   The stomach is unremarkable.  Small bowel loops
demonstrate normal caliber, wall thickness, and enhancement throughout.  The
colon and rectum are within normal limits.  The appendix is not visualized. 
Small amount of free fluid is present.

PELVIS: The urinary bladder and distal ureters are unremarkable.  A peritoneal
dialysis catheter is coiled in the pelvis with adjacent free fluid.

REPRODUCTIVE ORGANS: The uterus is anteverted and unremarkable.

LYMPH NODES: There is no retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymphadenopathy.  There
is no pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy.

VASCULAR: There is no abdominal aortic aneurysm.  Minimal atherosclerotic
disease is noted.

BONES: There is no evidence of worrisome osseous lesions or acute fracture. 
There is minimal retrolisthesis of L5 on S1

SOFT TISSUES: The abdominal and pelvic wall is within normal limits, noting a
peritoneal dialysis catheter which courses through the anterior abdominal wall
just left of midline.

IMPRESSION:


1. No evidence of diverticulitis or other significant enteric abnormalities.
2. Small locules of pneumoperitoneum and free fluid are likely the sequela of
peritoneal dialysis catheter use.
